basis: Clonal histiocytic neoplasm with explicit pulmonary disease parents; destructive bone lesions occur in approximately 30-50% of adults.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: destructive skeletal lesions affect approximately 30-50% of adults with Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

basis: Posthitis directly inflames the foreskin, a cutaneous fold. Infection or autoimmune causation is not inherent to the concept.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the inflamed structure is foreskin itself, which is skin; its genital location does not exclude a directly cutaneous disorder.

basis: Craniosynostosis, maxillary retrusion and intellectual disability define the syndrome. Open bite/high palate at 30-79% do not establish independent oral tissue damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: open bite and high palate occur in 30-79%, but describe craniofacial geometry without established dental injury or impaired oral function.

basis: Pontocerebellar hypoplasia defines the disorder. Respiratory insufficiency accompanying severe neurologic dysfunction does not establish intrinsic lung disease.

decisions.pulmonary: none: neonatal respiratory insufficiency is defining, but no intrinsic lung or airway lesion is established; neurologic respiratory failure alone is insufficient.

basis: Defined metabolic liver disease with neurodegeneration; skin disease 4/6 retained under primary cap. Dental defects ~50%, hearing loss and contractures 2/6 omitted by total cap.

decisions.hepatic: primary: the definition explicitly identifies a metabolic liver disease with iron overload; overt liver failure need not occur in 30% for primary status.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: ichthyosis/dermatitis affects 4/6; retained here because metabolic, hepatic and neurologic disease occupy the three primary slots.

basis: Inherited glycinergic startle disorder. Stiffness is neurologic; reflux, hiatus hernia and esophagitis reported at 80-99% are separate conditions rather than direct gut involvement.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: despite HPO frequencies of 80-99%, reflux/hiatus hernia and consequent esophagitis are separate diagnoses, not direct gastrointestinal injury by hyperekplexia.

basis: Severe intellectual disability and regression define syndrome; scoliosis/kyphosis occur in 30-79%. Oral and eyelid morphology lack established functional injury; reflux is separate.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: macroglossia occurs in 30-79% without demonstrated oral injury or dysfunction; feeding difficulties are symptoms and reflux is separately diagnosed.
decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis occurs in 30-79%, but the record establishes eyelid morphology without visual impairment or other damaging ocular disease.

basis: Hydrocephalus and pulmonary hypoplasia define the core syndrome; intestinal malrotation and limb/bone malformations each occur in 80-99%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: limb undergrowth and long-bone bowing occur in 80-99%; these are associated structural abnormalities alongside the defining brain and lung defects.

basis: Brucella suis infection; species-specific destructive osteoarticular involvement is not established at >=30%. Common arthralgia alone does not demonstrate joint damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: estimates from brucellosis overall do not establish >=30% destructive osteoarticular disease specifically for B. suis; arthralgia alone is insufficient.

basis: Leydig-cell dysfunction causes androgen deficiency; hypospadias is a structural urethral malformation reported in 80-99%. Delayed skeletal maturation alone does not establish bone damage.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias is a congenital urethral malformation reported in 80-99%; the renal axis explicitly includes the urethra.
